name: Argument Structure Profiling
description: Analyzes the unnatural rigidity, extreme predictability, and excessive telegraphing of discourse transitions within an argument framework.
mechanism: This method evaluates the architectural rigidity of an argument. LLMs are ruthlessly fine-tuned via RLHF to be extremely structured, safe, and easily readable to the lowest common denominator. This training inevitably forces them into textbook-perfect 'five-paragraph essay' templates. They heavily and predictably telegraph their every move using explicit discourse markers ('Firstly', 'Furthermore', 'Moreover', 'In conclusion'). Authentic human discourse, especially from professionals and experts, is far more organic and chaotic—humans weave claims together, overlap evidence, defer conclusions, or use implicit logical transitions rather than constantly signposting every single shift in thought like a traffic cop. By mapping the topological sequence of claims and transitional markers, the system identifies the overly mechanical, predictable, and 'paint-by-numbers' scaffolding typical of AI generation.
useCase: Detecting textbook-perfect, highly rigid argumentative essay structures that rely on repetitive transitional signposting ('Firstly... Secondly... Finally...') to string together claims.
strengths:
• Directly targets structural RLHF safety and flow alignment biases that are virtually inescapable for LLMs.
• Incredibly effective at detecting automated 'paint-by-numbers' essay and article generation.
• Highly resistant to simple synonym-swapping evasion techniques (e.g., replacing 'Firstly' with 'Initially' changes nothing structurally).
limitations:
• Highly susceptible to false positives when evaluating human writers who are purposefully taught to use rigidly structured essay formats (e.g., high school students, TOEFL/IELTS test-takers).
• Completely irrelevant and not applicable to narrative fiction or poetic texts where logical transitions do not exist.
• Less reliable on extremely short texts (under 100 words) where structural patterns cannot emerge.
parameters:
Analysis: Discourse Topology Mapping
Metric: Transition Marker Rigidity vs. Organic Implicit Shifts
Output: 0-100 Structural Rigidity Score
accuracy: High — 78-86%. Specifically powerful against standard unprompted LLM outputs ('Write an essay about...').

references.title: Biber, D. et al. (1999). Longman Grammar of Spoken and Written English. Pearson.

source: Biber, D. et al. (1999). Longman Grammar of Spoken and Written English. Pearson.
